title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook (2026)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's people operations best practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, ongoing performance management, and manager-facing guidance. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, engineering and product leaders, and people managers across the company.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time employees (FTEs), contractors (where noted), and interns unless a role-specific process is linked below.
- Includes: job requisitions, interview design and scorecards, offer and background check process, preboarding and 30/60/90 onboarding plans, performance cycles (quarterly check-ins + annual review), calibration, promotion guidance, and performance improvement paths.

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai).
- Escalation: For legal or compliance questions, escalate to Legal & Finance (finance-legal). For security or access exceptions, escalate to Security & Infra (security-and-compliance / eng-infra).

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)
Purpose: Reduce time-to-hire while preserving candidate quality and equitable evaluation.

Required steps (high-level):
1. Requisition & role definition
   - Create a Requisition in Workday with job family, level, compensation band, hiring rationale, and headcount approval.
   - Attach job description template and required interview skills.
2. Sourcing & screening
   - Recruiter screens for baseline qualification and culture fit using a 15-minute screen template.
   - Target metrics: initial screen within 72 hours of candidate submission.
3. Interview loop design (standard template)
   - Stage 1: Technical assessment (take-home or pair-coding depending on role) — scorecard focused on problem-solving, readability, and correctness. Timebox: 3–5 days.
   - Stage 2: Deep technical interview (1.0–1.5 hrs) — system design / runtime / performance for infra roles.
   - Stage 3: Cross-functional partner interview (30–45 min) — collaboration and communication.
   - Stage 4: Manager & bar-raiser (45 min) — team fit, leadership, decision-making.
4. Decision & calibration
   - Panel collects scorecards within 24 hours after loop. Recruiter coordinates debrief. Decision should include: hire/hold/no-hire, suggested level, and recommended comp band.
5. Offer approval & extension
   - Comp approval from Finance and Recruiting. Target offer issuance within 5 business days of final decision.
6. Background checks & acceptance
   - Standard background checks initiated after candidate accepts verbal offer. Final written offer contingent on successful check (per role policy).

Interview scorecard (required fields)
- Candidate name (string)
- Role and level
- Interviewer name
- Core competencies (1-5 rating): Technical competence, Problem solving, Communication, Ownership, Culture add
- Strengths (text)
- Risks / concerns (text)
- Recommendation (hire/hold/no-hire)

Unconscious bias & fairness checklist (required before decision)
- Cite evidence for each score.
- Avoid relying on non-job-relevant factors (e.g., university name, accent).
- If panel disagrees, request one additional interview with a neutral panelist.

Key metrics & SLAs
- Time-to-fill (requisition open -> offer accepted) target: median 35 days.
- Time-to-offer (final interview -> offer issued) target: 5 business days.
- Offer acceptance rate target: >= 75%.
- Diversity interview coverage: at least one diverse interviewer per loop when feasible.

2) Preboarding and onboarding
Preboarding checklist (to be completed before start date)
- HR: send welcome email, confirm start date, collect I-9/identity docs, benefits enrollment window.
- IT: create account(s) (Okta), provision Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, and GitHub access.
- Security: request device management enrollment and assign security training module (complete by day 7).
- Manager: send welcome message, first-week schedule, and 30/60/90 plan.
- Buddy assignment: designate a peer buddy with onboarding responsibilities.

First-week plan (example)
Day 0 (before start): paperwork completed, device shipped.
Day 1: Orientation (company mission, org structure), benefits overview, security onboarding, team meet-and-greet.
Day 2: Role-level ramp overview, environment setup, access checks.
Day 3: First small task assigned (low-risk code/doc change or onboarding project).
Day 4: Cross-team intro meetings (product/infra/ops).
Day 5: First-week recap with manager, set 30-day goals.

30/60/90 template (manager to co-author with employee)
- 30-day goals: access, small deliverable, relationship building.
- 60-day goals: independent contributions, larger deliverable, process familiarity.
- 90-day goals: measurable impact, ownership of a component or project, performance check-in scheduled.

Onboarding success criteria (examples)
- Access to all required systems by day 3.
- First production-facing PR or contribution by day 30 (role-dependent).
- Positive 30-day check-in resolution and documented next steps.

3) Performance and feedback cycles
Cadence
- Continuous feedback: encouraged via 1:1s and Slack; formal notes kept in manager docs.
- Quarterly check-ins: manager and employee review progress vs objectives; update 30/60/90 or OKRs.
- Annual performance review: written self-reflection + manager review + calibration panel.

Quarterly check-in template
1. Accomplishments since last check-in (3 bullets)
2. Roadblocks and support needed (2 bullets)
3. Skills to develop (1-2 items)
4. Updated goals and success metrics (clear, measurable)

Annual review workflow
- Week -4: People Ops opens review cycle, managers receive calibration materials.
- Week -2: Employee submits self-reflection (guidance prompts provided).
- Week -1: Manager submits review and proposed rating and comp recommendation.
- Week 0: Calibration meeting with manager group and People Ops to align ratings and leveling.
- Week +1: Manager delivers review to employee, updates career plan.

Calibration & leveling guidance
- Use concrete examples from the review period that map to role rubric.
- If a rating is changed during calibration, manager will meet the employee within 5 business days to explain rationale.

Promotion and compensation cycles
- Promotion process: manager nominates, includes evidence (projects, impact, leadership), peer feedback, and manager + skip-level endorsement. People Ops coordinates final approval.
- Compensation reviews: annual band refresh + spot adjustments for exceptional contributions. Finance approval required for out-of-band increases.

Performance improvement (PIP) process (when required)
- Trigger: repeated documented performance gaps after coaching (usually >= 2 check-ins) or significant single incident.
- Steps:
  1. Manager documents expectations and gaps in writing and shares with employee.
  2. People Ops consults to ensure fairness and compliance.
  3. 30–90 day PIP is created with concrete milestones, owner, and check-in cadence.
  4. At PIP conclusion: outcomes = success (remove plan), extension (if good faith progress and documented rationale), or separation.
- Legal/HR involvement required before any separation.

4) Manager playbook (practical how-tos)
Running effective interviews
- Prepare: read candidate CV, define role-specific anchors, and bring 3-5 focused questions.
- During interview: timebox, ask for thought process, take structured notes on the scorecard.
- After interview: submit scorecard within 24 hours and summarize evidence for rating.

Onboarding a new hire (manager checklist)
- Week -1: Welcome note and start plan. Confirm buddy and schedule.
- Week 0: Ensure all access and hardware are ready. Meet daily for first week.
- First 30 days: assign a runnable first task, schedule regular feedback, and introduce to key partners.

Coaching and feedback conversations
- Use SBI (Situation-Behavior-Impact) model for clear, actionable feedback.
- Frequency: weekly 1:1s recommended for new hires and direct reports on PIP; biweekly for established contributors.
- Documentation: Capture outcomes and action items in manager docs; share summaries with employee after critical discussions.

Offboarding (brief)
- Follow standard offboarding checklist: revoke access (Okta, GitHub, AWS), collect equipment, complete final payroll and benefits steps, and exit interview. People Ops to confirm.

5) Templates and examples
- Interview scorecard (one-line example): "Technical: 4/5 (clear algorithmic understanding); Communication: 3/5 (concise but lacked structure); Recommendation: hire"
- 30/60/90 snippet: "30d: complete onboarding project X; 60d: own service Y's bug triage; 90d: deliver feature Z and own rollout"

6) Compliance, security, and data privacy notes
- All candidate and employee data must be stored in HRIS (Workday) or People Ops-approved tools only.
- Background checks and I-9s handled per policy in security-and-compliance.
- Access exceptions must be approved by Security with a documented justification.

7) Continuous improvement and metrics to track
- Quarterly review of hiring funnel conversion metrics (applied -> screen -> onsite -> offer -> accept).
- Onboarding satisfaction survey at day 30 and day 90.
- Manager effectiveness survey annually.
- People Ops to publish a quarterly summary to the Leadership Team with trends and recommended changes.
